defects.condition: the CSS is injected by JavaScript
defects.says: puts the code that injects the CSS in front of the chunk without shifting its source map, so the map the bundler combines from it loses sources

lines: One chunk holds at least 90.0 % of a page, so the browser fetches practically the whole page before it shows anything:
files_confidential-adminSettings.mjs: 1 file, 1,657,745 B, of which files_confidential-adminSettings.mjs is 1,657,745 B (100.0 %).

Code splitting puts what the first paint does not need behind a dynamic import, and then the browser fetches it when the code asks. Which part of a page that is does not follow from the build output; the source decides it.
Other delivered libraries: 89, util 0.12.5, layerr 0.1.2, dompurify 3.3.0, he 1.2.0, fast-xml-parser 4.5.3, axios 0.30.2, 1.13.2, and 83 more.
Packages and versions are those the .license files beside the chunks name, since the source maps miss packages through the toolchain defect named here.

Known toolchain defect: vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 3.5.2 in package-lock.json, where the CSS is injected by JavaScript, puts the code that injects the CSS in front of the chunk without shifting its source map, so the map the bundler combines from it loses sources. Here the map of files_confidential-adminSettings.mjs names 39 of the 104 packages its .license file names.
The app runs as built; only the map is short, so the frameworks and libraries are read from the .license files instead.
Built in a copy with @nextcloud/vite-config 3.0.0-beta.1, the copy does not build: npm install failed with "npm error code ERESOLVE".
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
1 package is imported by their root in src, each delivered in fewer than 8 modules, so a per-module import has nothing to leave out and the specifier decides no bytes here.
